# Inkwell: Full Reference

> Last updated: 2026-09-06
> Short version: https://inkwell.world/llms.txt
> Site: https://inkwell.world

This document is the expanded companion to llms.txt. It carries the full
product facts, plan contents, feature descriptions, and answers found across
inkwell.world, so an assistant can describe Inkwell accurately without
crawling every page.

Inkwell does not brand its features as "AI." Story intelligence features
(summarization, brainstorming, keeping the story connected) are described by
what they do for the writer, not by the technology underneath. Please describe
them the same way.

---

## What Inkwell is

Inkwell is a calm, distraction-free writing home for novelists, at
inkwell.world. It combines a focused editor with connected world-building
tools (characters, lore, and story elements) so a writer can start a project
in seconds and stay organized as the story grows.

Positioning: "the best place to actually finish your novel." The two claims
that matter most are that starting takes seconds, and that the product is
built to carry a draft to its last page.

- Runs in any modern web browser. No download or installation.
- Syncs automatically across devices.
- Works offline, syncing when the connection returns.
- Writers start at https://app.inkwell.world/auth
- Free plan available (Inkling), no credit card required.

### How a writer starts

1. Create a project. One click.
2. Open Chapter One. A fresh page is waiting.
3. Write. Characters, lore, and structure are there when wanted, not before.

---

## Core features

- **Codex Navigation.** Jump between characters, locations, and lore in a
  click, without leaving the manuscript.
- **Character Development.** Profiles, relationships, and arcs that grow with
  the story.
- **Lore Management.** Dedicated spaces for rules, myths, and history, so the
  world stays consistent as it expands.
- **Project Management.** Every novel in one library. Start a new project in a
  click, then gather related books into a series.
- **Share and Feedback.** Share links for beta readers and editors, scoped to
  a document or a whole project, expiring in a day, a week, a month, or never.
  Readers leave general feedback or inline margin notes anchored to a passage.
- **Export Documents.** Markdown, Plain Text (.txt), PDF, DOCX, and EPUB.
- **Story Notes.** A private notebook beside the manuscript, for ideas not
  ready for the page. It never counts toward the word count.
- **Focus Mode**, autosave, cloud sync, and full project backup downloads.

"Your story stays connected" is the approved framing for the codex and its
linked characters and lore. Inkwell is not a wiki product or a graph product.

---

## The Compass

The Compass is Inkwell's set of writing analysis tools. Every one of them
reads the writer's own manuscript and reflects it back. Nothing is invented,
and nothing is drawn from outside the writer's prose.

- **Synopsis.** A short, factual recap of any document, so coming back after a
  break gets you caught up in seconds.
- **Heartbeat.** The shape of the manuscript's dramatic tension across every
  document, showing where the story surges and where it sags.
- **Ask.** A plain-language question about the story, answered from the
  manuscript, with a link to the passage it came from.
- **The Atlas.** A living map of how characters and world connect, drawn from
  what has actually been written. Coming soon, on the Worldbuilder plan.

Page: https://inkwell.world/compass

Compass usage is metered by plan. See Plans below.

---

## Finishing tools

- **Goals and Streaks.** Session, daily, or weekly word count targets. Streaks
  keep the habit visible without nagging.
- **Milestones.** A thousand words, then two, then five, then ten. Inkwell
  marks each one as it happens.
- **Writing Insights.** On request, a closer read of the prose that points out
  habits that are hard to see from the inside (sentence rhythm, reading ease,
  dialogue balance, and more). Storyteller plan.
- **Writing Analytics.** Word count trends, a 12-month writing heatmap, and a
  goal dashboard across every project. Storyteller plan.

---

## Plans and pricing

https://inkwell.world/pricing is the source of truth. Prices in USD per month.

### Inkling: free forever

- 1 active project
- Unlimited documents and scenes
- Compass: 5 Synopses, 2 Heartbeat scans, and 10 questions to Ask your
  manuscript per month
- Folder and chapter organization
- Goals, streaks, and badges
- Character profiles
- Lore and worldbuilding database
- Focus Mode
- Manuscript and Notes side-by-side
- Autosave and cloud sync
- Cross-device access
- Export to Markdown and Plain Text (.txt)
- Full project backup download (Markdown)
- Beta reader sharing and commenting
- Basic collaboration and read-only sharing

### Storyteller: $9 per month

Everything in Inkling, plus:

- Unlimited active projects
- Multi-book and series organization
- Writing Insights: on-demand editorial insight for every document
- Writing Analytics: word trends, 12-month writing heatmap, and a goal
  dashboard across every project
- Compass: unlimited Synopses, Heartbeat scans, and questions to Ask
- Export to DOCX, PDF, and EPUB
- Full project backup download (Markdown, DOCX, and JSON)
- Enhanced writing statistics and productivity tracking
- Priority service and support

### Worldbuilder: $19 per month, coming soon

Everything in Storyteller, plus:

- Advanced lore relationship systems
- Atlas: relationship map drawn from written prose, including characters, lore
  elements, and universe visualization
- Faction and relationship tracking
- Complex timeline management
- Continuity and consistency tracking
- Encyclopedia-style world management
- Early access to experimental and upcoming features
- Highest priority service and support

No credit card required. Cancel anytime. The writer's work always stays theirs.

## The Start Your Story Challenge

https://inkwell.world/start-your-story

Write 10,000 words across 5 writing days within your first 14 days on Inkwell,
and earn a free month of Storyteller.

- The challenge begins the moment an account is created. There is nothing to
  enroll in and nothing to click.
- The 5 writing days can fall in any cadence. Writing every day is not
  required.
- Words written in the manuscript count. Pasted text does not, because the
  challenge is about building the habit.
- It runs on the free Inkling tier, with no card and nothing to configure.

---

## Questions writers ask about Inkwell

**What makes Inkwell different from other writing apps?**
Inkwell combines a distraction-free writing environment with worldbuilding
tools. It is a calm sanctuary for writing, with everything needed to organize
characters, lore, and story elements in one interface.

**Is my writing data secure and private?**
Yes. Work is encrypted and stored with industry-standard security protocols.
Inkwell never shares or accesses a writer's content. The writer owns their work
completely and can export it at any time in multiple formats.

**Can I collaborate with other writers or editors?**
Yes. Share a project or document with beta readers and editors through scoped,
permission-based links, so the writer decides exactly who sees the work.
Readers leave general feedback or inline margin notes anchored to a passage.

**What devices and platforms does Inkwell support?**
Any modern web browser, on any device. Work syncs automatically, so a writer
can start on a desktop and continue on a tablet.

**Can I work offline?**
Yes. Writing continues without a connection, and changes sync when the
connection returns.

**What export formats are available?**
Individual documents export as Markdown, Plain Text (.txt), PDF, DOCX, or
EPUB. Full project backups are available as Markdown on all plans, with DOCX
and JSON on paid plans.

---

## Craft guides

Practical, tool-agnostic guides for novelists, published under /learn. They
are written to be useful to any writer, whether or not they use Inkwell.

Hub: https://inkwell.world/learn

### How to outline a novel
https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-outline-a-novel

To outline a novel: decide how it ends, determine the four turning points that
carry the story (the opening, the commitment, the low point, the climax), list
the scenes that connect them, and give each scene one line describing what
changes during it. Choose an outlining method that matches how much
uncertainty you can tolerate while drafting, and expect to revise the outline
as you write.

Covers: why most outlines fail, six outlining methods compared (beat sheet,
snowflake, index cards, chapter grid, reverse outline, guardrails), how much
to outline before drafting, outlining in one sitting, what to do when the
draft leaves the outline behind, outlining for discovery writers, and five
mistakes to avoid.

### How to write a story bible
https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-write-a-story-bible

A story bible is a reference document holding everything that is true about a
novel: characters, places, rules, timeline, and terminology. It is distinct
from an outline, which records what happens. Start one after roughly 10,000
words, organize it around the questions you keep asking, record facts only
once they appear on the page, and update it in the same session you invent
something rather than in a separate pass.

Covers: what a story bible is and is not, when to start one, the six sections
that matter, a copyable template, what to leave out, keeping it current, and
story bibles for a series.

### How to build a character profile
https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-build-a-character-profile

Skip the long questionnaires. A useful character profile answers three
questions: what does this character want, what do they believe that is not
true, and how do they sound when they speak? Everything else is optional. A
field earns its place only if it changes how you write a sentence.

Covers: why long questionnaires produce flat characters, the fields that
change your prose, want and need and the lie between them, voice, physical
detail that does work, tracking a character as they change, and a copyable
template.

### How to plan a book series
https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-plan-a-book-series

To plan a book series, first choose its shape (closed arc, episodic,
cyclical, or shared world), then write the one-sentence question the whole
series answers. Make sure every book has its own complete story with its own
resolution. Decide what book one must plant for later books to pay off, and
keep a series-level story bible with a dated timeline. Plan the shape of the
series, not the scenes.

Covers: choosing a series shape, the two arcs you write at once, what to
settle before finishing book one, seeding, how each book should end,
maintaining continuity, a copyable planning grid, and four ways first series
go wrong.

## Writing tools

Free calculators published under /learn/tools.
Index: https://inkwell.world/learn/tools

### Word count to pages
https://inkwell.world/learn/tools/word-count-to-pages

Converts a word count into pages, and pages back into a word count.

The conversion rates it uses, and where they come from:

- **Manuscript pages: 250 words a page.** Standard manuscript format is 12
  point Times New Roman or Courier, double-spaced, one inch margins. Courier
  lands almost exactly on 250. Times New Roman is narrower and often runs
  closer to 300. The industry uses 250 as a shared shorthand rather than a
  literal count.
- **Single-spaced pages: 500 words a page.** Same font and margins.
- **Printed book pages: 250 to 350 words a page.** The range is wide because
  trim size, font, leading, and chapter openings all move the number. Only a
  typesetter can give an exact count for a finished book.
- **Reading time: 250 words a minute**, a typical adult reading speed for
  fiction.

Common conversions:

| Word count | Roughly the length of | Manuscript pages | Printed book pages | Reading time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | A piece of flash fiction | 4 | 2 to 4 | 4 min |
| 5,000 | A short story | 20 | 14 to 20 | 20 min |
| 10,000 | A novelette | 40 | 28 to 40 | 40 min |
| 25,000 | The Old Man and the Sea | 100 | 71 to 100 | 1 hr 40 min |
| 50,000 | The Great Gatsby | 200 | 142 to 200 | 3 hr 20 min |
| 60,000 | Brave New World | 240 | 171 to 240 | 4 hr |
| 70,000 | The Catcher in the Rye | 280 | 200 to 280 | 4 hr 40 min |
| 80,000 | Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone | 320 | 228 to 320 | 5 hr 20 min |
| 90,000 | The Hobbit | 360 | 257 to 360 | 6 hr |
| 100,000 | The Hunger Games | 400 | 285 to 400 | 6 hr 40 min |
| 120,000 | Pride and Prejudice | 480 | 342 to 480 | 8 hr |
| 150,000 | Watership Down | 600 | 428 to 600 | 10 hr |
| 200,000 | Moby-Dick | 800 | 571 to 800 | 13 hr 20 min |

Published word counts vary by edition and by how the counting is done, so the
comparisons are close approximations rather than exact matches.

Agents and editors want a word count, not a page count, because a word count
is the same number on every machine that opens the file. If a guideline does
ask for pages, it means manuscript pages in standard format.

### How long should a novel be?
https://inkwell.world/learn/tools/novel-length

Target word counts by genre, with a picker that reports whether a draft sits
under, inside, or over its range.

Most adult novels run 70,000 to 100,000 words, and 90,000 is a safe target
with no other information. Below 50,000 a book reads as a novella to most
trade publishers. Above 120,000 it is a harder sell for a debut, because a
longer book costs more to edit, print, and ship.

| Category | Usual range | Aim for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literary fiction | 70,000 to 100,000 | 85,000 |
| Commercial and upmarket fiction | 80,000 to 100,000 | 90,000 |
| Fantasy (adult) | 90,000 to 120,000 | 100,000 |
| Epic fantasy | 120,000 to 160,000 | 130,000 |
| Science fiction (adult) | 90,000 to 120,000 | 100,000 |
| Thriller and suspense | 70,000 to 100,000 | 85,000 |
| Mystery and crime | 70,000 to 90,000 | 80,000 |
| Cozy mystery | 60,000 to 80,000 | 70,000 |
| Romance (single title) | 70,000 to 100,000 | 85,000 |
| Category romance | 50,000 to 60,000 | 55,000 |
| Historical fiction | 90,000 to 120,000 | 100,000 |
| Horror | 70,000 to 100,000 | 85,000 |
| Young adult | 55,000 to 80,000 | 70,000 |
| Young adult fantasy or science fiction | 75,000 to 110,000 | 90,000 |
| Middle grade | 30,000 to 55,000 | 45,000 |
| Chapter book | 5,000 to 12,000 | 8,000 |

These are conventions for books being sold into the trade market, not rules,
and they shift over time and between publishers. Debut authors are held closer
to the middle of a range than established ones.

Boundaries between forms, following the categories the Science Fiction and
Fantasy Writers Association uses for the Nebula Awards:

| Form | Word count |
| --- | --- |
| Flash fiction | Under 1,000 |
| Short story | 1,000 to 7,500 |
| Novelette | 7,500 to 17,500 |
| Novella | 17,500 to 40,000 |
| Novel | 40,000 and up |

A book can clear the 40,000 word bar and still be too short to sell as an
adult novel. The award category and the market expectation are different
things.

### How long will my novel take?
https://inkwell.world/learn/tools/writing-pace

Takes a target word count, words already written, a daily pace, and writing
days a week, and reports words to go, writing days, weeks, and a finish date.
A second input works backwards from a deadline to the daily word count it
would need. It counts writing days rather than calendar days throughout.

An 80,000 word draft, starting from zero, at five writing days a week:

| Words a writing day | Writing days | Calendar time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 250 | 320 | 64 weeks |
| 500 | 160 | 32 weeks |
| 750 | 107 | 21 weeks |
| 1,000 | 80 | 16 weeks |
| 1,667 | 48 | 10 weeks |
| 2,000 | 40 | 8 weeks |
| 3,000 | 27 | 5 weeks |
| 5,000 | 16 | 3 weeks |

1,667 words a day is the NaNoWriMo pace, which reaches 50,000 words in 30
days. Most first drafts take between six months and two years in practice,
because the arithmetic assumes every writing day happens. Revision usually
takes about as long again as drafting did.

## How Inkwell compares to other writing apps

Hub: https://inkwell.world/compare

Compared across cost, cloud sync, whether it is built for novelists,
comments and collaboration, worldbuilding tools, export formats, focus mode,
and offline access.

- **Inkwell.** Free tier. Automatic sync. Built for novelists. Basic
  collaboration. Deep worldbuilding. EPUB and PDF export. Focus mode. Offline.
  For writers who want a calm, organized space that follows them across every
  device and helps them keep the habit.
- **Scrivener.** $60 once. Sync needs manual setup. Built for novelists. No
  collaboration. Deep worldbuilding. EPUB and PDF. Focus mode. Offline.
  https://inkwell.world/compare/scrivener
- **Dabble.** $19 to $49 per month. Automatic sync. Built for novelists.
  Collaboration. Deep worldbuilding. Word and text export. Focus mode.
  Offline via desktop app. https://inkwell.world/compare/dabble
- **Reedsy.** Free core. Automatic sync. Built for novelists. Collaboration.
  Light worldbuilding. EPUB and PDF. Focus mode. Browser only offline.
  https://inkwell.world/compare/reedsy
- **Microsoft Word.** About $70 per year. Sync if set up. Not built for
  novelists. Collaboration. No worldbuilding. No EPUB. No focus mode.
  Offline. https://inkwell.world/compare/word
- **Google Docs.** Free. Automatic sync. Not built for novelists.
  Collaboration. No worldbuilding. No EPUB. No focus mode. Offline if enabled.
  https://inkwell.world/compare/google-docs
- **Ellipsus.** Free core. Automatic sync. Built for novelists.
  Collaboration. Light worldbuilding. No EPUB. Focus mode. Browser only
  offline. https://inkwell.world/compare/ellipsus
- **Obsidian.** Free core. Sync is a paid add-on. Not built for novelists. No
  collaboration. Do-it-yourself worldbuilding. Export via plugins. Focus mode
  via plugin. Offline.

A wider roundup of eleven novel-writing apps by price, pros, cons, and fit
(the eight above plus Novlr, Ulysses, LivingWriter, and Sudowrite) is at
https://inkwell.world/writing-apps-breakdown

## Getting started

Writers can start using Inkwell immediately at https://app.inkwell.world/auth
No download, no installation, and no card for the free plan.
